nonblocking_findings: F1 [Low, nonblocking] Both runners floor LIVE_CALL_START to whole seconds with date +%s, then compare native millisecond time.created against start*1000 (review-run.sh:1212, judge-run.sh:962). A stale terminal message created after that floor but before call entry can pass the freshness filter. P4E-2 uses created=1 and does not test this sub-second boundary. Capture a millisecond call-start timestamp or use another precise current-call marker, then add a failing-first fixture. Route to backlog row 4.15 under the PM cap. | CONTEST kept: the F20 timing-sensitive failure demonstrates the edge, while the named A-F1 adversarial case remains skipped; retain the finding as backlog work.

F2 [Low, nonblocking] When message.sessionID matches the created session but info.sessionID names another session, both selectors accept the message because the top-level value wins (review-run.sh:1218-1219; judge-run.sh:968-969). P4F-2 pins this conflicting-owner case as a skip. Native messages omit these optional owner fields, and the endpoint is session-scoped. Route to backlog row 4.15 under the PM cap.

F3 [Low, nonblocking] Both selectors treat any non-empty finish string other than exact tool-calls as terminal and accept any finite completed timestamp, including negative or reversed values (review-run.sh:1235-1238; judge-run.sh:985-988). P4F-3 skips these malformed-metadata cases. Native values are expected to be valid, so this is a malformed-response edge. Route to backlog row 4.15 under the PM cap.
